title: Annotatio IV §.V: Acts 2 — new converts devoted to Apostolic teaching and koinonia
pass_a_gloss: From Acts 2:42, where Jews newly converted to Christianity by Peter’s sermon, and the first of all, are set forth as proskarterountes, i.e. assiduously and continually attending not only to the didachē of the Apostles — Apostolic Doctrine, even concerning the Supper — but also to the koinōnia set out by the Apostle in 1 Cor. 10 from v. 16 to 20 inclusive.
pass_b_english: Acts 2:42: Jews newly converted by Peter’s sermon — the first of all — kept attending assiduously (proskarterountes).
Not only to the Apostles’ teaching (didachē), including on the Supper, but also to the koinōnia Paul sets out in 1 Cor. 10:16–20.
source_text: Ex Act. 2. 42., ubi Judæi, mediante Petri sermone, ad Christianismum noviter conversi, iidemque primi omnium, proskarterountes, i. e. assiduè atque perpetuò incumbentes sistuntur, non tantum didachē tōn Apostolōn, Doctrinæ, etiam de Cœna, Apostolicæ, sed & tē koinōnia ab Apostolo 1. Cor. 10. à vers. 16. ad 20. inclusivè expositæ.
